params.body:
## What

Step 2 of three for the Mix page. Step 1 (#193, dashboard#52) was the looking. This is the saying: on a row of the mix someone at the desk says **too much**, **fine** or **too little**, in one sentence, and it is kept with who and when.

A wish is not a setting. Nothing reads it to change what is collected. That is the reason to do this before any dial exists: first learn what the desk actually wants, then build the dials they ask for, and have every dial answer to a sentence somebody wrote.

## How

- `packages/core/mix-wishes.mjs`: table `mix_wishes`, append-only. The latest wish per (axis, row) stands, earlier ones stay: "too little" followed three weeks later by "fine" is the record that something was done.
- "Too much" and "too little" need a sentence; "fine" does not. Without the sentence it is a mood, and the sentence is what a dial will answer to.
- `POST /mix/wishes {axis, key, wish, note}` in a new `routes-mix.mjs`. Only a signed-in person: the static API token is refused here, and a probe token cannot write anywhere.
- `GET /mix/wishes?axis=` gives everything said, latest first.
- `GET /mix` now carries `wishes`, the standing wish per row. The counts stay cached for five minutes; the wishes are read fresh, so a wish is on the page the moment it is written.

`test/mix-wishes.test.mjs` pins the refusals, who said it, latest-stands-and-history-stays, and the route.

## Next

The dashboard side (three words per row and the sentence) follows in its own PR. Step 3, the dials, only after people have used this.
params.title: A wish on a row of the mix: too much, fine, too little, in a sentence
